newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai oil crushers buy Oct soybeans, trade active.
newsitem.headline: Thai oil crushers buy Oct soybeans, trade active.

text.p: Thailand's grains and oilseeds market was active this week as some players, alarmed by a supply-related rise in Chicago futures, rushed in to cover demand, trade sources said on Monday.

A major Thai oil crusher bought 50,000 tonnes of South American soybeans this week for October shipment, a trader said. Another crusher also made inquiries but no firm orders were placed so far, traders said.
Soymeal was also active although buying was hand-to-mouth. Feedmills and end-users bought about 20,000 tonnes of soymeal over the week for July-August shipments.
"Actually, most nearby demand is covered. Perhaps this is a knee-jerk reaction on some buyers' part to the recent rise in Chicago," said a Bangkok trader.
"But those who were sidelined believed prices could drop further," he said.
Agri-business giant Chareon Pokphand was said to have made enquiries for a large quantity of soymeal for November-December shipments.

"But whether the firm bought or not we don't know. When CP buys, normally it's a hush-hush deal and the market in many cases will know only when cargoes are declared for arrival," said another trader from a US house.
The latest agriculture ministry crop forecasts drew mixed reaction from the grains and oilseed market and barely affected prices.

Corn traders were sceptical at the 1997/98 forecast which revised production down slightly to 4.52 million tonnes from 4.53 million. They said despite the revision, the figure may still be exaggerated and the actual output should not exceed 4.0 million tonnes.
"Normally, the government's corn forecast is higher than it should be as they try to discourage imports," said one local trader.

"We heard there is drought in some corn producing areas. Moreover, farmers in some major corn producing provinces have turned to ginger and other crops which offer better returns this year," he added. Thailand sets import quotas for corn on yearly, depending on demand and supply.

A marginal upward revision in the soybean output projection had virtually no affect on the market. The Agriculture Ministry put the 1997/98 (April-March) crop at 397,000 tonnes against 383,628 projected earlier. This is not adequate to meet demand expected to exceed one million tonnes and Thailand will have to continue importing.
Local soymeal firmed slightly to around 9.80-9.85 baht a kg this week. Corn prices edged down to 4.55 baht a kg in thin trade as most of the 200,000 tonnes imported had arrived, traders said.
